title: EPA 608 Core practice test
description: Free EPA Section 608 Core practice questions. Every answer is explained and linked to the EPA page or the section of 40 CFR Part 82 it comes from.

questions.question: A technician assembles a split air-conditioning system on site and charges it with 4 pounds of refrigerant. Does it fit EPA's description of a "small appliance"?

options.A: Yes, because its charge is under five pounds
options.B: No, because a small appliance must be fully manufactured, charged and hermetically sealed in a factory
options.C: Yes, because every air conditioner counts as a small appliance
options.D: No, because a small appliance must hold less than one pound of refrigerant

questions.explanation: EPA describes a small appliance as one that is fully manufactured, charged and hermetically sealed in a factory with five pounds or less of refrigerant. A system assembled and charged on site fails the factory condition, whatever its charge size.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: A contractor with no certified technician on staff wants to buy refrigerant for use in its customers' appliances. Its manager offers to sign a promise not to vent it. Under EPA's sales restriction, may the seller go ahead?

options.A: Yes, because a signed promise not to vent satisfies the rule
options.B: No, because the buyer must be, or employ, a certified technician
options.C: Yes, if the contractor pays in advance
options.D: Yes, if the cylinder holds less than 30 pounds

questions.explanation: EPA states it is a violation to sell or distribute refrigerant for use in an appliance unless the recipient is, or employs, a certified technician, and sellers must verify this. A signed promise, payment terms or cylinder size do not replace that condition.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: A technician recovers refrigerant from one customer's rooftop unit and wants to charge it into a unit owned by an unrelated company. According to EPA's service practice requirements, what must happen to the refrigerant first?

options.A: It must be run through the filter-driers on the technician's recovery machine
options.B: It must sit in a recovery cylinder for 30 days
options.C: It must be reclaimed by an EPA-certified reclaimer
options.D: The second company must sign a statement accepting it

questions.explanation: EPA states that if recovered refrigerant changes ownership, it must be reclaimed by an EPA-certified refrigerant reclaimer. Moving it to an unrelated company is a change of ownership, so on-site cleaning or the new owner's consent is not enough.

source.title: EPA: Stationary Refrigeration Service Practice Requirements

questions.question: A property management company owns two office buildings. A technician recovers refrigerant from a unit in the first building. According to EPA's service practice requirements, where may that refrigerant go without being reclaimed?

options.A: Into a unit in the second building, because the same company owns it
options.B: Into a unit in a neighboring building owned by a different firm
options.C: Into any unit the same technician services that week
options.D: Into a cylinder sold to another contractor

questions.explanation: EPA allows recovered refrigerant to go back into the same system, or into other systems owned by the same person, without restriction. Sending it to a different owner is a change of ownership, which requires reclamation first.

source.title: EPA: Stationary Refrigeration Service Practice Requirements

questions.question: An EPA inspector visits a refrigeration contractor's shop while one of its certified technicians is out on a service call with the original wallet card. Under 40 CFR 82.161, what must be kept at the technician's place of business?

options.A: Nothing, because the wallet card travels with the technician
options.B: A letter from EPA confirming the certification
options.C: A copy of the technician's certificate
options.D: The technician's graded test answer sheet

questions.explanation: The rule states: "Technicians certified under this section must keep a copy of their certificate at their place of business." Carrying the original card on a job does not replace that copy, and the rule asks for the certificate, not an EPA letter or a test answer sheet.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How long must a technician keep a copy of their Section 608 certification?

options.A: Until three years after they are no longer operating as a technician
options.B: For one year after the test date
options.C: For five years after the test date
options.D: Only until they receive the plastic card

questions.explanation: EPA says to keep the copy until three years after you are no longer operating as a technician. The rule is tied to when you stop working as a technician, not to the test date.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: A technician earned Type II certification in 1995 and has not taken another Section 608 test since. According to EPA, what is the status of that credential today?

options.A: It lapsed after 20 years
options.B: It must be renewed by retesting with the original program
options.C: It covers only the refrigerants that were in use in 1995
options.D: It is still valid, because Section 608 certification credentials do not expire

questions.explanation: EPA states that Section 608 technician certification credentials do not expire. A credential earned in 1995 therefore has no renewal date and no cutoff tied to the refrigerants of that time.

source.title: EPA: Section 608 Technician Certification Requirements

questions.question: A technician has lost their Section 608 certification card. Who should they contact for a replacement?

options.A: The EPA Regional Office
options.B: The company that certified them, whose name is on the card
options.C: The refrigerant wholesaler where they buy refrigerant
options.D: Their state environmental agency

questions.explanation: EPA does not administer the tests or issue cards, and it does not keep a database of certified technicians. EPA tells technicians to contact the company that certified them, whose name appears on the card.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: A technician has passed the Core and Type I sections at a proctored, closed-book session and now wants Universal certification. According to EPA, what else is needed?

options.A: Nothing; Core plus Type I already counts as Universal
options.B: Two years of work under a Universal technician
options.C: Passing the Type II and Type III examinations, so that all levels have been passed
options.D: A written request to EPA for an upgraded card

questions.explanation: EPA states that to receive Universal certification, an individual must pass the examinations at all levels. Someone who has passed only Core and Type I still needs Type II and Type III; supervised work or a request to EPA does not substitute.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: Under EPA's regulations, how long do testing organizations have to issue test results after the date of the test?

options.A: Up to 7 days
options.B: Up to 30 days
options.C: Up to 90 days
options.D: Up to 1 year

questions.explanation: EPA notes that its regulations allow testing organizations up to 30 days from the date of the test to issue test results.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: Who issues Section 608 test results and certification cards?

options.A: The U.S. EPA
options.B: The test proctor at the end of the exam
options.C: The EPA-approved testing and certification organization that gave the test
options.D: The technician's employer

questions.explanation: EPA states that it does not administer the tests and does not issue test results or certification cards, and that proctors may not issue certification cards. Results and cards come from the EPA-approved testing and certification organization.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: Under EPA's rules, what is the longest time a person may be an apprentice, counted from the date of first registering?

options.A: Six months
options.B: One year
options.C: Two years
options.D: There is no limit

questions.explanation: EPA states that a person may only be an apprentice for two years from the date of first registering.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: Is Section 608 certification needed to add or remove refrigerant from a mini-split system as part of installation?

options.A: No, installation is exempt
options.B: Only if the system holds more than 50 pounds
options.C: Only for commercial buildings
options.D: Yes, Section 608 technician certification is required

questions.explanation: EPA states that adding or removing refrigerant from a mini-split as part of installation requires Section 608 technician certification.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: Section 608 technician certification is required to dispose of appliances, except for which type of appliance?

options.A: Small appliances
options.B: High-pressure appliances
options.C: Low-pressure chillers
options.D: Very high-pressure appliances

questions.explanation: EPA states that technician certification is required to dispose of appliances, except for small appliances (and motor vehicle air conditioners or MVAC-like appliances). High-pressure, very high-pressure and low-pressure appliances need a certified technician.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: EPA's safe disposal page places responsibility on the final person in the disposal chain to make sure refrigerant is recovered. Which kind of equipment does that responsibility cover?

options.A: Large chillers that technicians take apart on site
options.B: Equipment that enters the waste stream with its charge intact, such as household refrigerators and freezers or window air conditioners
options.C: Commercial rooftop units removed by service contractors
options.D: Only equipment that contains exempt refrigerants

questions.explanation: EPA explains that for equipment that enters the waste stream with its charge intact (for example motor vehicle air conditioners, household refrigerators and freezers, and window unit air conditioners), the final person in the disposal chain, such as a scrap metal recycler or landfill owner, is responsible for ensuring that refrigerant is recovered before final disposal. Large systems taken apart on site and rooftop units removed by contractors are not the equipment this responsibility describes.

source.title: EPA: Stationary Refrigeration Safe Disposal Requirements

questions.question: A scrap recycler receives a refrigerator carrying only an unsigned sticker that reads "refrigerant removed." According to EPA's safe disposal page, how should the recycler treat the sticker?

options.A: As full verification, because the sticker says the refrigerant is gone
options.B: As full verification, if the sticker is dated
options.C: As not acceptable verification; the recycler must still obtain a signed statement giving the name and address of the person who recovered the refrigerant and the date it was recovered
options.D: As full verification, if a certified technician applied it

questions.explanation: EPA's safe disposal page states that "EPA does not mandate or accept a sticker as a form of verification" that the refrigerant has been properly recovered prior to disposal. The final disposer must still obtain a signed statement that includes the name and address of the person who recovered the refrigerant and the date it was recovered; a date on the sticker or who applied it does not change this.

source.title: EPA: Stationary Refrigeration Safe Disposal Requirements

questions.question: A shop still uses a recovery machine built in 1991. Under EPA's service practice requirements, which requirement does the machine's age excuse it from?

options.A: Certification by an EPA-approved equipment testing organization
options.B: Use according to the manufacturer's directions
options.C: Use by a certified technician
options.D: The prohibition on venting refrigerant

questions.explanation: EPA states that, except for equipment manufactured before November 15, 1993, recovery or recycling equipment must have been certified by an EPA-approved equipment testing organization; all equipment must still be used according to the manufacturer's directions. A pre-1993 machine is excused only from the testing-organization certification, not from technician certification or the venting prohibition.

source.title: EPA: Stationary Refrigeration Service Practice Requirements

questions.question: For an oil change, EPA's service practice page sets a pressure limit before the system is opened. Instead of bringing the whole appliance to that limit, what other option does EPA describe?

options.A: Draining the oil into an open container while the system runs
options.B: Draining the oil into a receiver that is evacuated or pressurized to no more than 5 psig
options.C: Changing the oil at full system pressure if the job takes under 15 minutes
options.D: Venting the vapor charge first so the oil drains freely

questions.explanation: EPA says the appliance, or the receiver the oil drains into, must first be evacuated or pressurized to no more than 5 psig. Venting the charge or working at full pressure would break that rule.

source.title: EPA: Stationary Refrigeration Service Practice Requirements

questions.question: For leaking equipment, EPA says leaking components should be evacuated to the lowest level that can be reached without doing what?

options.A: Substantially contaminating the refrigerant
options.B: Running the recovery machine for more than one hour
options.C: Adding nitrogen to the system
options.D: Disconnecting the recovery hoses

questions.explanation: For leaking equipment, EPA says to evacuate leaking components to the lowest level attainable without substantially contaminating the refrigerant, and that level cannot exceed 0 psig. Run time, nitrogen use or hose handling is not the test.

source.title: EPA: Stationary Refrigeration Service Practice Requirements

questions.question: EPA's technician fact sheet gives carbon dioxide, nitrogen and water as examples of refrigerants exempt from the refrigerant management requirements. Where does it point technicians for the full list?

options.D: Appendix D to Subpart F

questions.explanation: EPA's technician fact sheet gives carbon dioxide, nitrogen and water as examples of exempt refrigerants and points to 40 CFR 82.154(a) for the full list. Section 82.161 covers technician certification, 82.157 leak repair and Appendix D certifying programs.

source.title: EPA fact sheet: Refrigerant Management Requirements, What Technicians Need to Know

questions.question: EPA's Core test topics link the destruction of ozone to chlorine. In which refrigerant families do the topics say chlorine is present?

options.A: HFCs only
options.B: HFCs and HCFCs
options.C: CFCs only
options.D: CFCs and HCFCs

questions.explanation: EPA's Core test topics list the destruction of ozone by chlorine and the presence of chlorine in CFC and HCFC refrigerants. HFCs contain no chlorine, and limiting the list to CFCs leaves out HCFCs.

source.title: EPA: Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics

questions.question: In the ozone-depletion potential (ODP) comparison in EPA's test topics, which family has a higher ODP than HFCs but a lower ODP than CFCs?

options.A: HCFCs
options.B: CFCs
options.C: HFCs
options.D: None; the three families have the same ODP

questions.explanation: EPA's test topics state that CFCs have a higher ozone-depletion potential than HCFCs, which in turn have a higher ODP than HFCs. That places HCFCs between the other two families.

source.title: EPA: Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics

questions.question: EPA's Core safety topics name two gases that should not be used for leak detection. Which pair is it?

options.A: Oxygen and compressed air
options.B: Nitrogen and helium
options.C: Nitrogen and oxygen
options.D: Compressed air and nitrogen

questions.explanation: EPA's Core safety topics include the use of nitrogen rather than oxygen or compressed air for leak detection. Any pair that includes nitrogen names the gas the topics recommend.

source.title: EPA: Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics

questions.question: A technician plans to connect a nitrogen cylinder straight to a system for a pressure test, with nothing else in the line. Which equipment do EPA's Core safety topics say belongs with nitrogen?

options.A: A vacuum pump and a micron gauge
options.B: A pressure regulator and a relief valve
options.C: A refrigerant scale and a recovery cylinder
options.D: A refrigerant identifier and a sight glass

questions.explanation: EPA's Core safety topics include the use of a pressure regulator and relief valve with nitrogen. Connecting the cylinder with neither device in the line leaves out both items.

source.title: EPA: Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics

questions.question: Besides the risks of overfilling refrigerant cylinders, EPA's Core safety topics cover the difference between which two kinds of cylinders?

options.A: Steel cylinders and aluminum cylinders
options.B: Nitrogen cylinders and oxygen cylinders
options.C: Reusable recovery cylinders and disposable cylinders
options.D: Liquid-only cylinders and vapor-only cylinders

questions.explanation: EPA's Core safety topics include the risks of filling cylinders more than 80 percent full and the difference between reusable recovery cylinders and disposable cylinders. Cylinder metal or gas type is not the distinction the topics draw.

source.title: EPA: Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics

questions.question: The Section 608 definitions sort appliances into low-, medium-, high- and very high-pressure classes by a refrigerant's liquid phase saturation pressure. At what temperature is that pressure taken?
questions.explanation: Each pressure-class definition uses the saturation pressure at the same temperature; for example, a medium-pressure appliance uses a refrigerant with a liquid phase saturation pressure "between 45 psia and 170 psia at 104 °F." The 85 °F figure belongs to the boiling-point test for pressurizing low-pressure appliances in 82.156, not to these definitions.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The definition of an MVAC-like appliance says it is not intended to cover appliances that use which refrigerant?
questions.explanation: After describing open-drive compressor appliances that cool the compartment of off-road vehicles, the definition states: "This definition is not intended to cover appliances using R-22 refrigerant." No other refrigerant is named in that exclusion.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the Section 608 definitions, which parts of an appliance make up its "refrigerant circuit"?

options.A: Only the compressor and the condenser
options.B: Every part of the appliance, including the cabinet and the wiring
options.C: Only the parts that hold liquid refrigerant
options.D: The parts that are normally connected to each other, or separated only by internal valves, and are designed to contain refrigerant

questions.explanation: Refrigerant circuit means "the parts of an appliance that are normally connected to each other (or are separated only by internal valves) and are designed to contain refrigerant." The definition is not limited to two components or to liquid-holding parts, and it does not reach the cabinet or wiring.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does the rule mean by "recovery efficiency"?

options.A: The percentage of refrigerant in an appliance that is recovered by a piece of recovery and/or recycling equipment
options.B: The number of pounds of liquid a recovery machine moves per minute
options.C: The percentage of moisture and acid a recycling machine removes
options.D: The share of a reclaimer's incoming refrigerant that meets appendix A

questions.explanation: Recovery efficiency means "the percentage of refrigerant in an appliance that is recovered by a piece of recovery and/or recycling equipment." It measures how much of the charge is captured, not speed, cleaning performance or reclaimer output.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The definition of "reclaim" refers to the specifications in appendix A. Which industry standard are those specifications based on?

options.A: AHRI Standard 740-2016
options.B: AHRI Standard 700-2016
options.D: ARI Standard 740-1993

questions.explanation: Reclaim means to reprocess recovered refrigerant to all of the appendix A specifications "(based on AHRI Standard 700-2016, Specifications for Refrigerants)" that apply to that refrigerant. The 740 standards and UL 1963 are named in 82.158 for testing recovery and recycling equipment.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The definition of an MVAC-like appliance, such as the air conditioning on a farm tractor, sets what limit on its full charge of refrigerant?

options.A: 5 pounds or less
options.B: 50 pounds or more
options.C: 20 pounds or less
options.D: 2 pounds or less

questions.explanation: The rule defines an MVAC-like appliance as an open-drive compressor appliance "with a full charge of 20 pounds or less of refrigerant" used to cool the compartment of off-road vehicles or equipment. It names agricultural and construction vehicles as examples.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How does the definition of "appliance" treat a system that has multiple independent refrigerant circuits?

options.A: The whole system counts as one appliance
options.B: Only the largest circuit counts as an appliance
options.C: The system counts as an appliance only if all circuits share a compressor
options.D: Each independent circuit is considered a separate appliance

questions.explanation: The appliance definition states: "each independent circuit is considered a separate appliance." The rule does not treat the whole multi-circuit system as a single appliance.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A hotel's own maintenance employee, not an outside contractor, removes a component from the refrigerant circuit of the hotel's rooftop air conditioner. How does the definition of "technician" treat this employee?

options.A: As a technician, because removing components can violate the refrigerant circuit and in-house personnel are covered
options.B: As outside the definition, because only outside contractors can be technicians
options.C: As outside the definition, because work on the owner's own equipment is not covered
options.D: As a technician only if the rooftop unit is a small appliance

questions.explanation: The definition lists "adding or removing components" among activities reasonably expected to violate the integrity of the refrigerant circuit, and says "Technicians could include but are not limited to installers, contractor employees, in-house service personnel, and owners and/or operators of appliances." Being on staff, or working on the owner's own equipment, does not take the employee outside the definition.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the rule's definition, connecting and disconnecting hoses and gauges to measure pressures is:

options.A: Considered opening an appliance in all cases
options.B: Not considered "opening an appliance"
options.C: Considered opening an appliance only on low-pressure appliances
options.D: Considered opening an appliance if the hoses stay connected for more than 15 minutes

questions.explanation: "Opening an appliance" means any maintenance, service, repair or disposal that would release refrigerant to the atmosphere. The rule states that connecting and disconnecting hoses and gauges to measure pressures, add refrigerant, or recover refrigerant "are not considered" opening an appliance.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Besides removing a compressor, condenser, evaporator or auxiliary heat exchange coil, which work counts as "major" maintenance, service or repair?

options.A: Uncovering any opening for more than 5 minutes
options.B: Uncovering an opening of more than 1 square inch of flow area for more than 60 minutes
options.C: Uncovering an opening of more than 4 square inches of flow area for more than 15 minutes
options.D: Uncovering an opening of more than 10 square inches of flow area for any length of time

questions.explanation: Major maintenance, service or repair includes work that involves "uncovering an opening of more than four (4) square inches" of flow area for more than 15 minutes. The other size and time combinations do not appear in the definition.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A technician recovers a non-exempt refrigerant into a cylinder and later knowingly releases it outdoors. Under the rule, this release is:

options.A: Allowed, because the refrigerant was already removed from the appliance
options.B: Allowed as a de minimis release
options.C: Allowed if certified recovery equipment was used
options.D: A violation of the venting prohibition

questions.explanation: The rule states that the knowing release of a class I, class II or non-exempt substitute refrigerant "after its recovery from an appliance is a violation of the venting prohibition." Having already recovered the refrigerant does not make a later release acceptable.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.154, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For a release of a non-exempt refrigerant to count as de minimis under the venting prohibition, which situation can make it qualify?

options.A: It happens while the required service practices, certified recovery machines, technician certification and reclamation requirements are all observed
options.B: It is less than one pound of refrigerant
options.C: The technician reports it to EPA within 30 days
options.D: It happens outdoors

questions.explanation: Except for exempt substitutes, releases are de minimis only if they occur when the applicable practices are observed and "recovery and/or recycling machines that meet the requirements in § 82.158 are used whenever refrigerant is removed from an appliance," with the technician certification and reclamation provisions also observed (or when subpart B is followed). The rule sets no size, reporting or outdoor test.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.154, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: In which uses is ammonia an exempt substitute under the venting prohibition?

options.A: In any application
options.B: In commercial or industrial process refrigeration or in absorption units
options.C: Only in household refrigerators
options.D: Only in motor vehicle air conditioners

questions.explanation: The list of exempt substitutes includes "Ammonia in commercial or industrial process refrigeration or in absorption units." Unlike carbon dioxide, nitrogen and water, ammonia is not exempt "in any application."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.154, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A refrigerant seller sells to a company that is not itself certified but employs a certified technician. Besides the invoice, what record must the seller keep?

options.A: A copy of every employee's driver's license
options.B: The buyer's most recent tax return
options.C: The documentation the buyer provided to show it employs a certified person
options.D: A photograph of each cylinder sold

questions.explanation: Where the buyer employs a certified person, "the seller must keep the documentation provided by the buyer to demonstrate such employment." The rule does not ask for licenses, tax returns or photographs.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.154, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: In which case may used refrigerant be sold or transferred for use as a refrigerant without first being reclaimed by a certified reclaimer?

options.A: When it is sold to any business that owns appliances
options.B: When it has passed once through a filter-drier
options.C: When it is sold by a technician to a different customer
options.D: When it is transferred between a parent company and one of its subsidiaries

questions.explanation: Among the exceptions to the rule on selling used refrigerant is refrigerant "being transferred between or among a parent company" and one or more of its subsidiaries. Selling to an unrelated buyer is not one of the listed exceptions, so that refrigerant would have to be reclaimed first.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.154, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What is the largest percentage of the refrigerant a certified reclaimer may release during the reclamation process?

options.A: 1.5 percent
options.B: 0.5 percent
options.C: 3 percent
options.D: 5 percent

questions.explanation: Persons reclaiming used refrigerant for sale to a new owner must "Release no more than 1.5 percent of the refrigerant during the reclamation process." The other percentages do not appear in the reclaimer requirements.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.164, Reclaimer certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What deadline does the rule set for reclaimers to send EPA their annual report on the material they received and the refrigerant they reclaimed?

options.A: December 31 of the same calendar year
options.B: February 1 of the next calendar year
options.C: July 30 of the next calendar year
options.D: April 15 of the next calendar year

questions.explanation: Reclaimers must report to EPA "annually by February 1 of the next calendar year." The report covers the material sent to them by refrigerant type, the mass of each refrigerant reclaimed and the mass of waste products.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.164, Reclaimer certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When a refrigerant reclamation business changes owners, what deadline does the rule set for the new owner to certify with EPA?

options.A: No deadline, because the old certificate transfers with the business
options.B: Within one year of the change
options.C: Within 30 days of the change
options.D: Within 90 days of the change

questions.explanation: The rule states "Certificates are not transferable," and the new owner must certify with EPA "within 30 days of the change" that they will meet the reclaimer certification requirements. The old owner's certificate does not carry over, and the rule sets no one-year or 90-day period.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.164, Reclaimer certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For reclamation purposes, what does the rule mean by a "batch" of refrigerant?

options.A: All refrigerant a reclaimer receives in one calendar month
options.B: All refrigerant recovered from one appliance
options.C: One shipment of recovered refrigerant sent by a technician
options.D: A single bulk cylinder of refrigerant after all reclamation is complete, before packaging or shipping

questions.explanation: A batch is defined as "a single bulk cylinder of refrigerant after all reclamation has been completed" prior to packaging or shipping to the market. It is not defined by time period, by appliance or by incoming shipment.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the technician certification rule, what may EPA require a certified technician to demonstrate, and where?

options.A: Their ability to perform proper procedures for recovering and/or recycling refrigerant, at their place of business
options.B: Their knowledge of the EPA test bank, at an EPA Regional Office
options.C: Their brazing skills, at a trade school
options.D: Their refrigerant purchase records, at their supplier's store

questions.explanation: The rule says the Administrator "may require technicians to demonstrate at their place of business their ability to perform proper procedures for recovering and/or recycling refrigerant." Failure to demonstrate or to use the equipment properly may lead to revocation or suspension of the certificate.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Technicians who maintain, service or repair MVAC-like appliances must hold which certification?

options.A: Type I only
options.B: Type II, or certification under 40 CFR part 82, subpart B
options.C: Type III only
options.D: No certification, because MVAC-like appliances are exempt

questions.explanation: The rule says technicians who service MVAC-like appliances "must either be certified as Type II technicians" or be certified under 40 CFR part 82, subpart B. Only the disposal of MVAC-like appliances is exempt from certification, not their service or repair.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under what condition is a registered apprentice exempt from the technician certification requirement?

options.A: When the apprentice has passed the Core section only
options.B: When the apprentice works only on weekends
options.C: When the apprentice is closely and continually supervised by a certified technician
options.D: When the apprentice's employer files a notice with EPA

questions.explanation: Apprentices are exempt provided the apprentice "is closely and continually supervised by a certified technician" during work that could release refrigerant. The rule also makes both the supervising technician and the apprentice responsible for the apprentice's compliance.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A person wants to take the certification test orally. How must they request this?

options.A: By asking the proctor on the day of the test
options.B: By phone at least 10 days before the test
options.C: By writing to EPA at least 60 days before the test
options.D: In writing to the program at least 30 days before the test, explaining why

questions.explanation: A test may be given orally to anyone who requests it "in writing, to the program at least 30 days before" the scheduled exam, and the request must explain why it is being made. The request goes to the certification program, not to EPA or the proctor on test day.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: After technicians finish a certification test, Appendix D requires the program to give them a paper hand-out or electronic message. Which item must it contain?

options.A: When they should expect to receive their score and, if they passed, their certification card
options.B: Their score on each individual question
options.C: A copy of the questions they were asked
options.D: The correct answers to the test

questions.explanation: The hand-out must include the program, its contact information, the proctor's name and contact information, and "When they should expect to receive their score and, if they passed, their certification card." Appendix D also requires programs to keep test questions and answer keys confidential.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under Appendix D, what is the only benefit a proctor may receive from the outcome of the testing?

options.A: A bonus for each applicant who passes
options.B: A fee for proctoring
options.C: A share of the certification card fees
options.D: Free certification for themselves

questions.explanation: Appendix D states: "The proctor may not receive any benefit from the outcome of the testing other than a fee for proctoring." It adds that proctors cannot know in advance which questions are on the tests they proctor.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)
